what_it_does: This paper addresses a type of attack called a backdoor attack on AI (neural network) models, where a hidden trigger causes the model to misbehave on demand. Most such attacks require the attacker to already have access to the model or some extra data — this work instead embeds the backdoor purely during the data-collection phase, before any model is even trained, by secretly poisoning the training data. The clever twist is that the attack keeps itself hidden at first (very low success rate before deployment), then a separate step called machine unlearning — a technique normally used to make models forget specific data — is used after deployment to silently 'restore' the attack to full effectiveness. Because the dangerous behavior only appears after unlearning rather than during normal training evaluation, standard safety checks miss it.
